title: Atomic‐Scale Insights Into the Thermal Stability of High‐Entropy Nanoalloys

recollection.starting_material: guess: equiatomic or near-equiatomic multi‐element (five‐ or six‐component) alloy nanoparticles synthesized by inert‐gas condensation or wet‐chemical reduction
recollection.intervention: guess: systematic in situ transmission electron microscopy (TEM) heating experiments up to 800–1000 °C under vacuum or inert atmosphere
recollection.structure: guess: retention of single‐phase face‐centered cubic (FCC) nanoalloy with grain sizes ∼5–15 nm and slight surface segregation of low‐melting elements
recollection.mechanism: guess: high configurational entropy suppresses element diffusion and grain‐boundary migration, stabilizing the nanoalloy against coarsening and phase separation
recollection.results: guess: observed less than 10 % grain growth after heating to 800 °C for 2 h, an increase of the onset of coarsening by 200 °C compared with binary alloys, and activation energy for coarsening of ~2.5 eV

score.note: The recollection generically identifies in situ TEM heating under vacuum and a broadly similar temperature range, but misses the exact 298–973 K ramp and STEM/MD analysis. Its claimed FCC retention and slight segregation contradict the observed Au/Cu surface-shell formation, melting, evaporation, and poor stability. The proposed entropy-suppressed diffusion mechanism is the opposite of the paper’s active, surface-energy-driven diffusion. All quantitative claims are unsupported and miss the reported 22% size reduction at 973 K.
